content:
AOM Offer Ladder

Source of truth for what AOM offers at every stage of the sales pipeline. Written: 2026-03-12 | Author: Alex (Deal Architect) Decision: Zero-risk free-work offers are DEAD. See decisions/log.md 2026-03-12.

The Rule

No free filming. No free spotlight series. No free content production. Ever. In any outreach, at any stage. Free work signals desperation and commits production hours before revenue.

The offer is the conversation. Then the offer is knowledge. Then the offer is a paid engagement.

Stage 1: Cold Email (Email 1)

Goal: Open the door. Get a reply, not a sale.

What to offer: Nothing. The offer IS the conversation.

Format: Patrik's voice template (projects/jacob/voice-template.md is the source of truth). Short, human, specific to the prospect. References their actual work. No pitch, no case studies, no stats, no links.

For construction: Lead with trade recognition. "Your work looks solid. I can tell you guys care." That's it. AI mention stays 1-in-5, casual, almost an afterthought. Per the voice template.

For CPAs / professional services: Same human energy, different language. "I work with a few businesses in Phoenix on their operations" instead of "construction companies." Adapt the pitch line to their world.

For partnerships (CPAs, consultants, agencies): Peer-to-peer framing. "Your clients probably need visibility but don't have someone executing it. We do that. Might be worth a conversation."

What Jacob needs to know: Email 1 has no offer. No CTA beyond "if you ever want to talk shop, I'm around." No links. No attachments. No "check out our work." Just a person who noticed something and reached out.

Stage 2: Follow-ups (Email 2-3)

Goal: Stay present. Add value without committing production hours.

Timing: Email 2 at 5 days. Email 3 at 7 days after email 2.

Email 2: The Market Breakdown Offer

What to offer: "I was putting together a quick breakdown of what similar companies in Phoenix are doing for content and visibility. Want me to send it your way?"

What this actually is: A 30-minute research doc. NOT a custom audit. NOT a strategy deck. It's a 1-2 page summary showing:

  • What 3-5 competitors/peers in their market are doing on social, web, and content
  • Where they stand relative to those peers (presence, posting frequency, engagement)
  • 1-2 observations about gaps or opportunities (not prescriptions, just observations)

Why this works: It demonstrates knowledge without giving away the store. It takes 30 minutes of research, not a day of production. It positions AOM as someone who understands their market, not just another vendor. And it gives the prospect something genuinely useful.

What Jacob needs to know: If they say "sure, send it," Jacob (or Patrik) builds the market breakdown from publicly available info. LinkedIn, Instagram, Google reviews, their website vs. competitors. No tools, no fancy reports. Just a clean doc that shows we did the homework.

Email 3: The Short Bump

What to offer: Nothing new. Just presence.

Format: Even shorter than email 1. "Still thinking about what you guys are building. Let me know if you ever want to grab coffee." Or reference something they recently posted/built. Stay human.

What Jacob needs to know: Email 3 is not a pitch escalation. Same energy, shorter. If they haven't replied to 2 emails, a longer one won't help. Brevity is respect for their time.

Stage 3: Discovery Call (The Quick Scan)

Goal: Demonstrate expertise. Identify 2-3 gaps. Convert to paid engagement.

What to offer: A 30-minute "quick scan" call. Patrik reviews their current operations (content, web presence, internal workflows) and identifies 2-3 specific gaps. Could be content gaps, AI automation opportunities, or both.

Positioning: This is valuable, not free. Frame it as: "I usually charge for this, but I like what you're doing and I'd rather show you what I see than tell you." The scan is a demonstration of AOM's brain, not a freebie.

The $250 credit: If the prospect converts to a paid engagement (audit or retainer), $250 of the quick scan's value credits toward their first invoice. This incentivizes conversion without discounting. Don't lead with the credit in outreach. Mention it on the call: "By the way, if we end up working together, this conversation credits toward your first month."

What happens on the call:

  1. Patrik asks 5-6 questions about their business, team size, pain points
  2. Patrik pulls up their web/social presence live, shares observations
  3. Identifies 2-3 specific gaps (content cadence, web conversion, admin automation, follow-up systems)
  4. Recommends one of two paths (see Stage 4)
  5. No hard close. "Here's what I'd do if I were you. If you want us to do it, here's what that looks like."

For construction: The gaps are almost always: inconsistent social posting, no video of their work, website that doesn't convert, manual follow-ups eating time. Patrik speaks their language. "You're doing great work, nobody's seeing it."

For CPAs / professional services: The gaps are: no thought leadership content, manual client onboarding, no AI in their workflow, referral system that's word-of-mouth only. The scan naturally leads to the AI audit.

For partnership prospects (CPAs, consultants): The call is about alignment, not selling. "Your clients need X, we execute X. What would a referral arrangement look like?" Keep it reciprocal. "We send you clients who need accounting, you send us clients who need visibility."

Stage 4: Paid Entry Points

Two doors into AOM. Every prospect fits one or both.

Door 1: AI Audit ($2,500)

Who it's for: Business owners who said yes on the quick scan and have clear operational/AI gaps. CPAs, professional services, and any business with 3+ employees doing repetitive admin work.

What they get:

  • Full operational audit (current tools, workflows, pain points, team structure)
  • Gap analysis with prioritized recommendations
  • Custom AI implementation roadmap
  • ROI projections specific to their business
  • Deliverable: written audit report + 1-hour walkthrough call

Timeline: 1-2 weeks from kickoff to delivery.

Why $2,500: It's the price of certainty. They walk away knowing exactly what to fix and what it's worth, whether they hire AOM or not. The report is theirs to keep.

The $250 credit from the quick scan applies here. Net cost: $2,250.

Door 2: Creative Production Retainer ($3,000/month)

Who it's for: Construction companies (primary), any business that needs consistent content but doesn't have a team doing it. The prospect who responded to "we showcase your hard work."

What they get:

  • Social media management (posting, scheduling, engagement)
  • Monthly filming sessions (on-site content capture)
  • Video editing and production
  • Content strategy aligned to their business goals
  • Platforms: Instagram, LinkedIn, TikTok (as relevant)

Why $3,000/month: This is what serious social media management costs when it includes production. Anything cheaper is a freelancer posting stock images. AOM shows up with cameras.

For construction specifically: The pitch is simple. "You build incredible things. Nobody sees it unless you show them. We show them." Construction companies are sitting on a goldmine of visual content (job sites, before/after, crew, equipment) and nobody's capturing it.

Stage 5: Upsell Paths

Once they're in the door, both paths expand naturally.

From AI Audit ($2,500):

  • AI System Build ($5,000-$8,000): Implement the recommendations from the audit. Custom agent setup, workflow automation, dashboard access.
  • Platform Retainer ($1,500-$3,000/month): Ongoing AI operations platform. Multi-tenant dashboard, over-the-air updates, continuous optimization. This is the SaaS play.
  • Add creative production: Client sees the AI system working, trusts AOM, wants content too. Natural cross-sell to $3k/month retainer.

From Creative Retainer ($3,000/month):

  • Rate increase: $3,000 -> $3,500/month once consistent posting is established and results are showing (the Ambition pattern).
  • Add AI advisory: "You're spending 10 hours a week on follow-ups and scheduling. Want me to show you what an AI system could do?" Cross-sell to audit.
  • Add web development ($3,000-$5,000 one-time): Most construction companies have terrible websites. Once they see the content flowing, they want a site that matches. Natural project add-on.
  • Expanded services: Event coverage, documentary-style content, brand videos. Higher-ticket one-offs layered on top of the retainer.

The Full Stack Client

The dream client is on both paths: $3k/month creative + $2k/month platform = $5k/month per client. 10 full-stack clients = $50k/month. That's the real target behind the 15-client construction goal.

Vertical-Specific Notes

Construction Companies (Primary Target)

  • Lead with trade recognition, not technology
  • AI mention: 1 in 5 emails, casual ("I've been designing AI systems for businesses, pretty interesting although I don't know if that would work for you")
  • The value prop: "We help construction companies get noticed"
  • Entry point: creative retainer ($3k/month), not AI audit
  • Upsell to AI happens after trust is established (month 2-3)
  • Key pain points: nobody sees their work, inconsistent posting, website doesn't reflect quality of work, manual everything

CPAs / Financial Services (AI Advisory Target)

  • Lead with operational efficiency, not content
  • Timing: tax season makes this urgent (Q1 every year)
  • Entry point: AI audit ($2,500)
  • The pitch: "You're doing your clients' books manually. I can show you where 10 hours a week disappears and how to get it back."
  • Partnership angle: reciprocal referrals. "Your clients need visibility, we execute. Our clients need accounting, we send them your way."
  • Upsell: audit -> build -> platform retainer

Partnerships (CPAs, Consultants, Agencies)

  • Peer-to-peer, not vendor-to-client
  • Frame: "Your clients need X, we deliver X. Let's set up a referral arrangement."
  • Keep it reciprocal. AOM sends referrals back.
  • No discounts for referral partners. Full price, referral fee structure instead.
  • Discovery call is about fit, not selling. "Does this make sense for both of us?"

What This Replaces

  • Any email or outreach that offers free filming, free video, free content production, or free spotlight features
  • The "zero-risk" language from previous outreach concepts
  • Any offer that commits AOM production hours before a paid engagement is signed

Quick Reference for Jacob

Stage What to Offer Time Cost to AOM Revenue
Email 1 Nothing. Open the door. 0 $0
Email 2 Market breakdown doc 30 min research $0
Email 3 Nothing. Stay present. 0 $0
Discovery Call Quick scan (30 min) 30 min call $0 ($250 credit if converts)
Paid Entry A AI Audit 1-2 weeks $2,500
Paid Entry B Creative Retainer Ongoing $3,000/month
Upsell (AI) Build + Platform Ongoing $5-8k + $1.5-3k/month
Upsell (Creative) Expanded services + web Ongoing $3.5k+/month + project fees

This document is the source of truth for AOM's offer strategy. Jacob scales it. Patrik runs the calls. Alex updates it when the market or pricing shifts.
